day_shape: 59 items: fresh US Treasury sanctions on Türkiye-based Golden network, E3+US push IAEA board to refer Iran to UNSC, IDF signals Lebanon strike wave and clears Hezbollah tunnel, Netanyahu names regime-change as 'central mission', heavy Defa Press/IRIB war-messaging cycle.

threads.label: US financial pressure and IAEA referral push
threads.summary: The State Department announced Treasury sanctions on Türkiye-based Golden entities to cut Iranian regime revenue, while the US, UK, France and Germany pushed the IAEA board to refer Iran to the UN Security Council. Iran International reported Iran's London bank faces closure on 22 October if Britain does not renew its Treasury permission, and the Jerusalem Post highlighted Iraqi trade as a Tehran lifeline.

threads.label: Israel operations on Lebanon and Gaza fronts
threads.summary: The Jerusalem Post reported the IDF planned a series of strikes across Lebanon Friday evening, and the IDF said it had cleared a 'strategic' Hezbollah underground facility in southern Lebanon. The IDF also announced the killing of Nukhba company commander Muhammad Mahmoud Marshad al-Qadi in Khan Younis and dismantled 30+ weapon-production machines near Nablus.

threads.label: Regime war-narrative and armed-forces messaging
threads.summary: Defa Press and IRIB carried statements from the army spokesman Amir Akraminya claiming missiles and drones 'easily penetrated' US air defences within 15 minutes of American aggression, alongside air-defence commander Elahami and Friday-prayer leader Khatibi declarations of readiness. Defa Press also claimed Trump 'admitted' US failure against Iran in a GB News interview and framed the USS Abraham Lincoln as a symbol of American defeat.

threads.label: Netanyahu regime-change line and Tehran debate
threads.summary: Times of Israel reported Netanyahu saying Israel's 'central mission' is to topple the Iranian regime and that the goal was 'within reach', while Iran International described a Tehran debate over compromise versus continued confrontation. The Jerusalem Post also reported the Pentagon instructed personnel in August to stop calling operations against Iran 'Operation Epic Fury'.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz closure and energy market claims
threads.summary: Defa Press posted that Iranian armed forces have closed the Strait of Hormuz and framed global oil and China's green transition as consequences, while IRIB cited US Treasury Secretary Bessent saying he expects oil prices to fall to $40 after the confrontation with Iran. Tehran Refinery's manager said the new CCR unit would add roughly 1.5 million litres per day to petrol capacity as Pezeshkian discussed gradual consumption management.

events.title_en: State of the energy market after the Strait of Hormuz closure
events.summary_en: State of the energy market after the Strait of Hormuz closure. The closure of the Strait of Hormuz by Iranian armed forces has turned energy supply into a matter of strategic importance for all countries in the world. Six months after the start of Iran's regional war, oil exporters and importers continue to grapple with challenges created in the oil market following the closure of the Strait of Hormuz by Iranian armed forces; a crisis that, despite grave consequences for the energy market, has led to significant revenue increases for some major oil companies. Before the start of American and Israeli attacks on Iran and the entry of West Asia into a war with an uncertain end, even the possibility of closing the Strait of Hormuz seemed unlikely.

events.summary_en: Martyrdom of border guard in Paveh. Reza Daraii Emarati, sergeant first class of the border guards of the border city of Paveh, was martyred in a clash with an anti-revolutionary opposition group. China's green path to end dependence on fossil fuels, following the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and amid rising energy consumption, has faced widespread challenges. In the first half of 2026, coal's share in China's energy mix fell below 50 percent for the first time, reaching 49.7 percent. This is while renewable energy's share exceeded the 40 percent mark, reaching 41.2 percent. In other words, one kilowatt-hour out of every four kilowatt-hours of electricity generated in China was provided from renewable sources. Chinese media called this moment a 'historic turning point' and the beginning of a real transition from coal-based production to coal-free production.
